commit_subject: Draft North Carolina PIT taxable-income boundary
description: promotes North Carolina 2026 personal income tax to the exact taxable-income boundary

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix pipeline computed liability from structure the cited sections do not contain -- a bracket base plus a caller-supplied marginal rate above a bracket floor and a subtracted nonrefundable credit under 105-153.7, which imposes a single flat percentage on North Carolina taxable income and says nothing about brackets or credits -- and derived 'North Carolina taxable income' as AGI minus a supplied standard deduction while its own proof excerpt from 105-153.5(a) says the taxpayer may deduct 'either the standard deduction amount or the itemized deduction amount'.
triage.triage_notes: Read the pinned corpus text of us-nc/statute/105/105-153.7 (release us-rulespec-2026-07-19-dedup, provision sha e174d86f...): subsection (a) is a flat percentage table with no bracket base/floor, and credits live outside 105-153.7, so the pre-fix bracket-base + supplied-marginal-rate + supplied-credit construction and its 105-153.5(a) grounding had no basis in the cited provisions; the fix removes nc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax entirely, re-grounds nc_pit_pilot_taxable_income on a supplied completed-return boundary, and pins the rate by importing us-nc:statutes/105/105-153/7#individual_income_tax_rate instead of accepting it from the caller. Kind is the uncertain part, not whether meaning changed: unrepresented_clause is defensible for the omitted itemized/child-deduction alternative (the fix retracts the derivation rather than adding the clause), and wrong_entity_or_scope is defensible because the output surface moves from post-nonrefundable-credit liability to a before-credits target. A reviewer could also argue this is a deliberate pilot-contract redesign (the old rationale explicitly wired 'the same supplied-schedule form as the Arizona and Kentucky flat pilots') rather than a defect -- hence confidence 0.5. Corroborating evidence that it was treated as broken: known-validation-gaps.yaml drops this module's pending validate_failures waiver (issue 782) in this same commit. The commit body is empty; the PR body is generic ('Draft until required CI is green and current'). Follow-up commit d1ed1b594 'Repair NC TY2026 statute source backing' (2026-07-26) touches this pipeline again.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix pipeline claimed N.C. Gen. Stat. 105-153.7 as the source for a bracket-base-plus-marginal-rate-above-a-floor formula and a subtracted nonrefundable credit, but the pinned corpus text of 105-153.7 imposes only "a percentage of the taxpayer's North Carolina taxable income computed as follows" with a year table (After 2025 3.99%) and contains no bracket base, no bracket floor, and no credit; the statutory rate itself was a caller-supplied variable, so the module encoded none of the operative law it cited. The fix deletes the entire nc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax rule, drops the credit subtraction, and re-grounds liability as taxable income times the rate imported from the encoded 105-153.7 module under a pinned proof hash, which is exactly the untraceable_branch pattern (remove or re-ground structure with no basis in the cited source). I tried wrong_period_or_effective_date (the fix does add effective_to 2026-12-31 because subsection (a1) can change the rate in 2027) and unrepresented_clause (the pre-fix taxable-income rule hard-wired the standard deduction although its own 105-153.5(a) excerpt allows "either the standard deduction amount ... or the itemized deduction amount"), but both are secondary: the period bound is a consequence of baking in the imported rate, and the fix removes the deduction step rather than adding the missing alternative. Mechanical is ruled out because a rule is deleted, both surviving formulas change, and the input set collapses from five supplied values to one.
triage.verifier_notes: Provision verified through the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-19-dedup (corpus commit 9bcd834, body sha256 e174d86f...): 105-153.7(a) is a flat percentage with a year table (After 2025 3.99%), (a1) is a 2027+ rate-reduction trigger, (b) is withholding tables. Nothing in the section mentions brackets or credits, and the removed formula "nc_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_base + nc_pit_pilot_supplied_marginal_rate * max(0, nc_pit_pilot_taxable_income - nc_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_floor)" carried a proof atom whose 105-153.7 excerpt ("A tax is imposed for each taxable year on the North Carolina taxable income of every individual") does not support bracket mechanics. This change is multi-kind: alongside the untraceable structure it also (a) bounds both versions with effective_to 2026-12-31 for the (a1) 2027 trigger (wrong_period_or_effective_date flavor, but only because the rate is now baked in via import) and (b) retires an AGI-minus-standard-deduction derivation whose own 105-153.5(a) excerpt offered an either/or the encoding ignored (unrepresented_clause flavor, though the fix deletes rather than completes it). Confidence is 0.68 rather than higher because a substantial part of the change is architectural (moving the upstream boundary to caller-supplied state taxable income, importing rather than accepting the rate) and the PR reports population parity with a maximum absolute difference under one dollar, so a reviewer could read it as a precision/scope promotion; what defeats that reading is that the module already asserted 105-153.7 as the source for a credit and bracket structure the section does not contain. Second module in the commit (us-nc/statutes/105/105-153/7.yaml) was not assessed here.
